subject: The Raven
hook: THE RAVEN IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The raven that inspired Poe’s famous poem was a real taxidermied bird owned by Charles Dickens, now on display at the Free Library of Philadelphia
angle_support: The Free Library of Philadelphia has on display a taxidermied raven that is reputed to be the very one that Dickens owned and that helped inspire Poe's poem.
Poe based the poem in part on a talking raven in the 1841 novel Barnaby Rudge by Charles Dickens
title: The True Origin of Poe’s Raven
description: Edgar Allan Poe’s famous poem was inspired by a real-life pet raven owned by author Charles Dickens. You can actually visit the preserved specimen at the Free Library of Philadelphia.
narration: THE RAVEN IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a dark, supernatural omen birthed from Poe’s imagination. It was closer to a real, taxidermied pet that lived long before the poem was ever written. Edgar Allan Poe drew his chilling inspiration from Grip, the talkative bird owned by Charles Dickens. That very raven was preserved after death and now resides at the Free Library of Philadelphia for visitors to see today. The literary masterpiece started as a stuffed bird on a shelf.
